title: Drawings and Light
tagline: Draw a school three ways, then let the sun in through the windows.
grownUp: This mission is about three ways to draw a building: the plan from above, the section cut through the middle, and the elevation from the side. Architects draw all three so the building makes sense.
The sun and the windows are the light lesson. Let the Architect move the sun and see when the classroom gets bright or glary.
The Big Question has no right answer. Big windows for the waves and small windows for less glare are both good reasons.

steps.title: Three ways to draw a building
steps.text: Architects draw a building in three ways. A plan shows it from above, a section is a cut through the middle, and an elevation shows one side from outside.
steps.ask: If you were floating above your school, what would you see?

steps.title: Which drawing is from above?
steps.prompt: Which of these drawings shows the whole building from above?
steps.reveal: A plan is the drawing from above, a bit like a map of the rooms. A section cuts through the building to show the inside, and an elevation shows one side.

steps.title: Cut, look and light it
steps.intro: Look at the plan, slide the section through, look from the sea, then move the sun and give a classroom a sea window.

steps.title: Big windows or small?
steps.scenario: Should the classroom windows be big, to watch the waves, or small, to keep the sun's glare off the board? A third choice is roof windows that let light in from above.

options.label: Big windows for the waves
options.detail: You can see the sea and the sky, and the room feels open and bright.

options.label: Small windows for less glare
options.detail: Less sun shines straight at the board, so everyone can read the words more easily.

options.label: Roof windows
options.detail: Light comes down from above, so the room is bright without anyone looking straight at the sun.

steps.reveal: Architects think about the view, the glare and how much light a room needs. Some schools choose big windows with a view, and others choose small windows or roof lights.
steps.followUp: Which window would you choose for your classroom, and what would you like to look at through it?

steps.title: Torch through a card house
need: An empty cereal box or a card box
Scissors, with a grown-up to help
steps: With a grown-up, cut a few windows in the sides of the box. Make one of them big and one of them small.
In the dark room, shine the torch through the windows and watch where the light lands inside the box.
Move the torch to the side, then above the box, and see how the light changes. Talk about where the real sun would be.
steps.why: The torch is the sun. Cutting windows in different places shows how architects let light in and keep the glare out.

debrief: Which of the three drawings would you use to show a friend your school, and why?
